privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.s1_text: The following information provides a simple overview of what happens to your personal data when you visit this website. Personal data is any data with which you can be personally identified. This website does not set cookies, does not use any advertising services and does not create user profiles. I use Umami for anonymised reach measurement (see section 6).
privacy.s2_intro: The party responsible for data processing on this website is:
privacy.s3_text: This website is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany ("Hetzner"). When you visit this website, Hetzner processes various information, including your IP address, in order to deliver the website. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; I have a legitimate interest in the most reliable and secure presentation of my website. A data processing agreement (DPA) pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR has been concluded with Hetzner. Fonts and all other files of the website are loaded directly from this server; there is no connection to Google Fonts or any other font provider.
privacy.s4_intro: The hosting provider automatically collects and stores information in so-called server log files, which your browser automatically transmits. These are:
privacy.s4_li4: host name of the accessing computer
privacy.s4_outro: This data is not merged with other data sources. It is collected on the basis of Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR for the purpose of ensuring a technically error-free presentation and the optimisation of the website.
privacy.s5_title: 5. Contact form and contact by email
privacy.s5_p1: If you send me an enquiry via the contact form, the data you enter in the form (name, email address and your message) will be transmitted to a script on the server and forwarded to my email address (info@jensbaumann.com) for the purpose of processing your enquiry. I do not pass this data on without your consent.
privacy.s5_p2: The processing of this data is based on Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR (consent, which you grant via the checkbox) and Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR if your request is related to the performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures. The data you enter will remain with me until you ask me to delete it, revoke your consent, or the purpose for data storage no longer applies (e.g. after your request has been processed). Mandatory legal provisions – in particular retention periods – remain unaffected.
privacy.s5_p3: To protect against automated spam requests, the script checks whether an additional field that is invisible to humans has been filled in and how long it took to complete the form. In addition, the server stores a pseudonymised check value (hash) of your IP address together with the time of the request in order to limit requests to five per sender per hour. Entries older than one hour are no longer taken into account and are deleted automatically with the next request. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest in preventing misuse).
privacy.s6_p1: This website uses the web analytics service Umami Cloud, provided by Umami Software, Inc. (USA). The collected data is stored on servers in the European Union. Umami collects anonymised usage data such as pages visited, time spent on the site, referring website, approximate country of origin, device type, browser and operating system. This helps me understand how my website is used and improve it.
privacy.s6_p2: Umami does not set cookies, does not store any information on your device and does not create cross-device profiles. Your IP address is not stored; it is only used briefly to generate an anonymous, regularly rotating check value. I am not able to identify individual visitors.
privacy.s6_p3: The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; I have a legitimate interest in the anonymised analysis of user behaviour in order to optimise my website. The data is stored in the EU; however, as the provider is based in the USA, access from the USA cannot be completely ruled out. You can object to the collection by enabling the "Do Not Track" setting in your browser or by using a script blocker.
privacy.s7_text: For security reasons and to protect the transmission of confidential content, this site uses SSL/TLS encryption. You can recognise an encrypted connection by the "https://" in your browser's address bar and the lock symbol.
privacy.s8_intro: You have the following rights at any time:
privacy.s8_li1: the right to information about your stored data (Art. 15 GDPR)
privacy.s8_li2: the right to rectification of incorrect data (Art. 16 GDPR)
privacy.s8_li4: the right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
privacy.s8_li5: the right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
privacy.s8_li6: the right to object to processing (Art. 21 GDPR)
privacy.s8_li7: the right to withdraw consent given at any time (Art. 7 (3) GDPR)
privacy.s8_li8: the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR), for example the data protection authority of Lower Saxony (LfD Niedersachsen), which is responsible for me

duo.label: About me
duo.career_text: I created my first websites as a teenager. Designed in Photoshop, cut into pieces and put back together with HTML. Professionally, things went in a different direction for a while. Now I'm finally doing what I've always enjoyed most.
duo.cert_text: My training as a Fullstack Developer: I've completed the frontend module, and on the backend I work with Python and Django.

structure.then: Every day I planned who does what and when and what takes priority, while still selling myself.
structure.now: On Join I set up the project and folder structure. We divided the tasks together: I led the conversation and listened to who wanted to take on what. I also reviewed every pull request and only merged it once everything was right.

debugging.then: On the phone or in chat, in German or English: I had to work out step by step where exactly the problem was.
debugging.now: That's how I look for bugs today. On Videoflix I wrote the tests from the start so problems show up early.

customers.then: Customers often come in with a fixed idea. Only the right questions make it clear what they really want and, above all, need.
customers.now: Before I implement a feature, I ask myself whether it helps the user. That's why I dropped several ideas for this portfolio that looked nice but wouldn't have helped visitors.

testimonials.quote_2: Jens is a dedicated team player with great perseverance. Whether technical or tricky problems: he stays focused and is an asset to any team.
testimonials.quote_3: I can highly recommend Jens – a strong full-stack developer who delivers clean code and always finds great solutions. The collaboration is absolutely relaxed, reliable, and uncomplicated. I would work with him again at any time!

videoflix.role: The whole backend, developed on my own
videoflix.summary: Videoflix is a small video streaming platform, and I wrote its backend. It handles sign-up, email activation, login and password reset. When you upload a video, it automatically creates a thumbnail and converts the video into three quality levels: 480p, 720p and 1080p.
videoflix.implementation: Written in Python with Django and Django REST Framework. Everything runs in Docker, with PostgreSQL as the database and Redis. After an upload, the tasks go into a queue via Django RQ and are processed in the background. That way the heavy conversion doesn't block the server: FFmpeg creates the thumbnail and converts the video into HLS streams. The video list is cached in Redis so it loads faster.
videoflix.focus: The biggest pieces were the background jobs, the HLS streaming format and a secure login with JWT in HttpOnly cookies, including token refresh and a blacklist. I wrote the tests from the start, including real FFmpeg conversions. The backend runs on my own server behind nginx with HTTPS.

dabubble.summary: DABubble is a chat app for teams, with channels, direct messages and threads. New messages show up instantly without reloading the page. There were two of us. My part was the layout, the logic for chat and threads, and the notifications.
dabubble.role_fact: Layout, chat and thread logic, notifications
dabubble.implementation: Angular on the frontend, Supabase as the database. I implemented the layout from the given design and wrote the logic for chat and threads. New messages reach everyone right away through Supabase's realtime feature. On top of that came the notification feature.
dabubble.focus: The sidebar, the chat and open threads always had to be in sync. When a new message comes in, it has to show up correctly everywhere at the same time: in the chat, in the open thread and in the notifications. Honestly, that wasn't easy.

join.type: Kanban board built as a team
join.role: Project lead, dashboard, drag and drop
join.summary: Join is a Kanban board: you create tasks, assign them within the team and drag them across the columns. There were four of us, and I led the project.
join.role_fact: Project lead, dashboard, drag and drop
join.implementation: My main part was the overview dashboard. I also implemented the drag and drop for the board and created the legal pages. As project lead, I reviewed every pull request and either merged it or sent it back for changes.
join.focus: When four people work on the same code, you quickly notice how important clear Git agreements are. Towards the end I took some extra time to tidy up the code so it's consistent and easy to read.

coderr.role: The entire backend, on my own
coderr.summary: Coderr is a marketplace where providers offer digital services and customers can book them. I wrote the backend: it manages profiles, offers, orders and reviews and makes everything available through a REST API.
coderr.implementation: Python with Django and Django REST Framework. I split the project into several apps: sign-in and profiles, offers, orders, reviews and statistics. The data is stored locally in SQLite.
coderr.focus: The main focus was linking offers, orders and reviews in a sensible way and keeping the API well organised, split into serializers, views and permissions. Login works with tokens, and I tested with pytest and pytest-django.

kanmind.role: The entire backend, on my own
kanmind.summary: KanMind lets teams organise their tasks on Kanban boards. I developed the backend for it: boards, tasks, assignments, comments and reviews.
kanmind.implementation: Python with Django and Django REST Framework, split into two apps: one for registration and login, one for everything around the board, meaning boards, tasks, comments and permissions. The data is stored locally in SQLite.
kanmind.focus: The API has to reflect how boards, tasks and comments relate to each other, and only show people what they're allowed to see. On top of that come token login and separate endpoints for tasks assigned to you or waiting for your review.

el-pollo-loco.role: Built on my own in three weeks
el-pollo-loco.summary: In El Pollo Loco, the main character collects coins and salsa bottles to beat the final boss. I developed the game on my own in three weeks.
el-pollo-loco.implementation: Everything in plain JavaScript, without a framework or game engine. I wrote my own game loop, plus classes for the main character and enemies that build on each other. Collision detection and sound are part of it too.
el-pollo-loco.focus: Collision detection gave me the biggest headache. When do you land on the enemy, and when do you get hit yourself? I had to try quite a few things before it worked properly.

pokedex.role: Built on my own in two weeks
pokedex.summary: A Pokémon encyclopedia that loads its data live from the PokéAPI. You can search for Pokémon and look at stats, evolutions and moves. I developed it on my own in two weeks.
pokedex.implementation: Plain JavaScript, set up with Vite and split into modules. I load the data with Fetch, and translations run through i18next. On top of that: several languages, a light and a dark mode, and a detail view that also works on phones.
pokedex.focus: The PokéAPI delivers lots of separate pieces of data, and the site still needed to stay fast. So I cache requests, the search only starts after a short typing pause, and I cancel requests that are no longer needed.

value.title: What's needed?
value.text: For every feature I ask myself: why do I need it, and what does the user get out of it? If it solves a real problem, it goes in.

design.title: What should it look like?
design.text: I design the project as a mockup first, down to the details.

tech.title: What do I use?

rules.title: Which rules apply?
rules.text: I decide what is allowed in the code and what isn't. It should be easy to understand so anyone can find their way around quickly. Clean code decides whether a project stays performant and maintainable.
